channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Trump on Israeli elections: I should stay out, but may endorse someone
item.description: US President declines to endorse a candidate in Israel's upcoming elections, but leaves open possibility he could do so later.

item.title: Teshuvah and improving the world
item.description: The power of teshuvah is not limited, it encompasses every domain of life, that of the individual and that of civilization as a whole.

item.title: Houthis claim to have fired ballistic missiles at Saudi ships in Bab al-Mandeb Strait
item.description: The Houthi military spokesman, Yahya Saree, confirmed that the rebel organization attacked a Saudi naval landing ship and four other military boats in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait with ballistic missiles.

item.title: Trump: Hamas agreed to disarm, Israel must cease strikes on Gaza
item.description: US President Donald Trump tells Fox News that he will bomb Oman if they 'get in the way,' insists Hamas will disarm.

item.title: Tunnel to Israel? Suspect caught digging near security fence
item.description: Border Police arrest Qalandiya resident suspected of working to dig tunnel to infiltrate Israel.

item.title: Shas officials jump ship
item.description: Three members of Shas' Kiryat Gat slate defect to rival Ahi party, citing Shas' opposition to IDF enlistment for haredim not studying in yeshiva.

item.title: 40 minutes of fear: Jews attacked in Barcelona
item.description: Seven Jewish tourists from France were attacked by hundreds at the port of Barcelona and subjected to 40 minutes of curses, spitting, and chants against Jews and Israel.

item.title: Public urged to pray for beloved rabbi
item.description: Family calls on the public to pray and increase Torah study and good deeds for Rabbi Shalom Pinchas Burstein. 'He is in need of great Heavenly mercy.'

item.title: Likud primaries: The battle heats up, Gotliv claims missing voting slips
item.description: 14,307 Likud members already exercised their right to vote in Likud primaries. Gotliv claims ballots without her name, Yoni Yosef withdraws candidacy, and Netanyahu expresses support for Osnat Zohar.

item.title: 80 cattle seized after disrupting IDF training
item.description: Border Police raid Golani live-fire zone after herds repeatedly entered military training areas, forcing IDF exercises to be disrupted or halted. Watch.

item.title: Arab leaders upset by Jewish visits to Temple Mount
item.description: High Follow-Up Committee delegation visits Temple Mount, Islamic Movement leader shares religious justification for Ra'am's efforts to join center-left government after elections.

item.title: Despite war, record crowds head for Uman
item.description: Over 45,000 Israelis expected to make annual pilgrimage to Uman Ukraine, despite closed Ukrainian airspace, martial law, and a grueling journey across the border.

item.title: The Arab vote in Israel-Legality, Morality and Security
item.description: The Israeli High Court has a long record of flouting the law when it comes to Arab parties’ participation in Knesset elections. But in the post-October 7th era, in which the vulnerability of the state was so vividly exposed, it is essential to vigorously enforce both the spirit and the letter of Clause 7(a) of the Basic Law: The Knesset. Opinion.

item.title: Israelis don't give up: Time is running out for survivors in Colombia earthquake
item.description: Col. Yossi Pinto, head of Israeli delegation to Colombia, describes the search for missing people one week after the earthquake, 'We have yet to find any survivors, but Israelis don't give up.'

item.title: The forthcoming elections and the unity of Am Yisrael
item.description: A house can contain people who are different from one another, each with his own character and his own way, and yet they are all living under the same roof. That is the picture we should have of Am Yisrael.

item.title: Trump’s Middle East gamble is unwinnable
item.description: Iran won’t come to the table and Hamas won’t disarm. But as luck would have it Iran, unsuspecting and all, can help Trump gain pole position. Opinion.

item.title: Couple marry at hospital so bride's critically ill mother can attend the ceremony
item.description: Michal and Tal had planned to get married a year from now, but Michal’s mother’s medical condition led them to move up the wedding and hold it at Shaare Zedek Medical Center.

item.title: Residents accuse: Tefillin, cash stolen after Samaria outpost demolition
item.description: Residents returning to Givat Tel Talpiot following violent demolition say religious items, credit card, and thousands of shekels missing, and belongings destroyed.

item.title: After robot hit, commander takes initiative: daring rescue under Russian drone threat
item.description: After two soldiers were wounded by FPV drones and the rescue robot was hit, company commander Vladislav Polsky went in without body armor, loaded them into a civilian pickup, and brought them to safety.

item.title: WSJ reveals: Iran's secret plan to escalate the war
item.description: Extremist elements in Iranian leadership decided to utilize ceasefire period granted by Iran-US memorandum of understanding to prepare for future conflict, Wall Street Journal report reveals.

item.title: The war we cannot afford to lose
item.description: Israel needs a doctrine of strategic prevention and overwhelming deterrence. We need to ensure that no potential coalition can ever become sufficiently confident in its ability to overwhelm Israel that it concludes an attack is worth the risk.

item.title: NY synagogues rethink security after attack
item.description: Jewish watchdog urges NYPD to increase officers in hot spots after synagogue attack.

item.title: Jaffa resident arrested on suspicion of vandalizing statues and crosses at city church
item.description:
Police arrested a Jaffa resident in his 20s on suspicion of vandalizing and causing extensive damage at the Church of Saint Anthony in the city.
During the incident, several statues in the church compound were knocked over and broken, while broken crosses were found on the floor and chairs. The suspect was arrested by police and taken to the station for further questioning.

item.title: Reports in Lebanon of Israeli strikes in the south of the country
item.description:
Lebanese Al Mayadeen TV, which is affiliated with the Hezbollah terrorist organization, reported a strike in the village of Al-Qantara in southern Lebanon overnight.
Artillery strikes were also reported in the area of the village of Al-Mansouri and in the Wadi al-Saluki area in southern Lebanon.

item.title: Reports of Air Force strikes in eastern Gaza City
item.description: According to reports from Gaza, Air Force aircraft carried out targeted strikes this morning against targets and areas in eastern Gaza City.

item.title: Far-right leader, called 'most dangerous man in Germany,' could become state premier
item.description: German weekly Der Spiegel calls AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund 'Germany’s most dangerous man,' who could become the far-right party’s first state premier in Saxony-Anhalt, marking a historic turning point in German politics.

item.title: Fox News poll: Republican Mike Rogers leads progressive Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan
item.description: Fox News survey places Republican Mike Rogers ahead of anti-Israel Democrat Abdul El-Sayed 51% to 47% in Michigan's Senate contest.

item.title: American actress Hayden Panettiere passes away at 36
item.description:
American actress Hayden Panettiere has passed away at the age of 36. Panettiere was widely known for her roles in the hit US television series "Heroes" and "Nashville."
US media outlets reporting her death did not provide details regarding the cause or circumstances of her passing.

item.title: Iran advances law imposing prison terms for interviews with 'hostile' media
item.description: Iran's parliament approves a bill penalizing unauthorized interviews with hostile media with up to two years in prison, alongside strict curbs on foreign contact.

item.title: Zvi Yehezkeli slams Kushner’s meeting with Hamas officials: A slap in Israel's face
item.description: Middle East analyst Zvi Yehezkeli harshly criticizes Jared Kushner’s meeting with senior Hamas officials in Egypt: "The very occurrence of this meeting is a victory for Hamas - legitimizing and normalizing the group."
